title: Why Is Sea Limited Stock Falling, and is it a Buying Opportunity? SE Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate asks whether Sea Limited's fall is a buying opportunity after the stock topped $130 in August and crashed back below $76, near its 52-week low, after starting the year below $80. Sea runs three segments: e-commerce (Shopee), financial services and gaming. Gaming is the most profitable but the slowest growing at 15%, while the loan book grew 62% and Shopee gross merchandise value grew 28%, with total revenue up 48% in the latest quarter. Costs are rising sharply, a major headwind for Shopee, and there is concern the company is relaxing lending standards too aggressively, though management says AI is improving lending decisions and keeping risk low, which remains to be seen. Wall Street expects 18.6% EPS growth over the next several years, and cash flow from operations to sales of 18.8% is enough to fund growth. Shopee is expanding on an asset-light basis by renting facilities, and the balance sheet is strong with over $11.5 billion of cash and short-term investments against only $2.7 billion of long-term debt. On valuation, the forward P/E of 14.83 sits below expected EPS growth, and his DCF fair value is $104 per share versus a price just below $75, so the stock looks undervalued on both measures. He calls it a buying opportunity on the dip, a first tracked BUY for him, but warns it may take more than a year to recalibrate expenses, so it suits long-term investors with a horizon beyond 2027.
